newsitem.title: CHINA: Tung sworn in as Hong Kong's new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Tung sworn in as Hong Kong's new chief executive.

text.p: Billionaire businessman Tung Chee-hwa, 60, was sworn in early on Tuesday as the first chief executive of Hong Kong, since midnight a Special Administrative Region of China.

His right hand raised, Tung took the short oath facing Chinese Premier Li Peng at a ceremony attended by many foreign dignitaries but boycotted by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and British ministers.

London and Washington were showing their opposition to Beijing's decision to scrap the Legislative Council, elected in 1995 under British colonial rule, and replace it with an unelected provisional legislature.
Immediately after Tung's swearing-in, his new government -- 24 departmental secretaries led by Chief Secretary Anson Chan -- also took the oath.
Then the 60 members of the new provisional legislature were sworn in in their turn.
